title: Phulkari Darn-Stitch Embroidery
summary: Phulkari, "flower work", is the embroidery of Punjab in India and Pakistan: long darning stitches of untwisted silk floss are sewn from the back of a coarse handwoven cotton cloth, so that gold, cream, green and orange rows of stripes build diamonds, triangles and lattices.
howToPlay: Choose a floss colour and a stitch from the strip under the cloth.
Touch a square to darn it: the cloth reads the same turned half a circle, so the square at the opposite end is stitched with it.
Copy the small design shown above the cloth, then press Check.
rules: The cloth looks the same when turned half a circle, so each stitch you place is repeated at the opposite end.
Long stitches and triangles turn with the cloth, as the floss runs the other way on the far half.
A square counts only when its stitch and its floss colour both match the design; three stars need a nearly perfect copy.
heritageNote: Women across Punjab on both sides of the border have embroidered phulkari on handspun cloth for generations; the fully covered form is called bagh, "garden", and the craft is still worked in homes and cooperatives.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original bands after traditional darn-stitch layouts)
